Package common.core.subsystems

Class PivotMechanism

java.lang.Object
edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.SubsystemBase
common.core.subsystems.MechanismBase
common.core.subsystems.PivotMechanism
All Implemented Interfaces:
edu.wpi.first.util.sendable.Sendable, edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Subsystem
public class PivotMechanism extends MechanismBase
Rotates to an angle and holds it: arms, wrists, shooter hoods, turrets.

PID and feedforward run on the motor controller. The PivotMechanism.Orientation says which way it points at 0, which decides how gravity acts:

  • PivotMechanism.Orientation.FORWARD, PivotMechanism.Orientation.BACKWARD, PivotMechanism.Orientation.LEFT and PivotMechanism.Orientation.RIGHT (arms, wrists, hoods) swing up and down. Angles follow WPILib: 0 is level, pointing that way from the pivot, and positive is up. Feedforward is kS plus kG times the cosine of the angle, so kG is the voltage to hold it level.
  • PivotMechanism.Orientation.TURRET turns side to side. 0 is facing the front of the robot and positive is counterclockwise seen from above. Gravity doesn't act on it, so leave kG at 0.

The mechanism is assumed to be at startPosition when the robot turns on, and the encoder is reset to it. 


 // An arm in degrees that starts hanging straight down, can swing from -90 to 90, and weighs 4 kg
 arm = new PivotMechanism("Arm", Orientation.FORWARD, ARM_CONFIG, ARM_GAINS, 1,
     -90, 90, -90, Math.PI / 180, 0.6, 4, DCMotor.getKrakenX60(1), new NAR_TalonFX(ARM_ID));
 arm.setSetpoint(45);

For a wrist driven directly on an arm, a hood on a turret, or an arm on an elevator, see setParent(MechanismBase).

  • Constructor Details

    • PivotMechanism

      public PivotMechanism(String name, PivotMechanism.Orientation orientation, NAR_Motor.MotorConfig motorConfig, PIDFFConfig gains, double tolerance, double minPosition, double maxPosition, double startPosition, double radiansPerUnit, double lengthMeters, double massKg, edu.wpi.first.math.system.plant.DCMotor motorType, NAR_Motor... motors)
      Parameters:
      name - Name shown on Shuffleboard and in logs
      orientation - Which way it points at 0, which decides whether gravity acts on it
      motorConfig - Applied to every motor; its distance factor sets the position units
      gains - PID and feedforward gains, in volts per position unit
      tolerance - How close to the setpoint counts as MechanismBase.atSetpoint()
      minPosition - Lowest allowed setpoint
      maxPosition - Highest allowed setpoint
      startPosition - Where it is when the robot turns on
      radiansPerUnit - Radians per position unit, e.g. Math.PI / 180 for degrees
      lengthMeters - Pivot to the far end of the moving part, with any telescope on it retracted; used only in simulation
      massKg - Mass that moves, including everything mounted on it, e.g. the telescope and wrist on an arm; used only in simulation
      motorType - Model of one motor, e.g. DCMotor.getKrakenX44(1); used in simulation, and to hold up what telescopes on it move out
      motors - Every motor on the mechanism. The first is the leader.

    • setParent

      public void setParent(MechanismBase parent)
      Mounts this on another mechanism, e.g. a wrist driven directly on an arm, an arm on an elevator, or a wrist on the end of a telescoping arm. Its 3D pose moves with the parent's.

      On another pivot, its position is relative to the parent, with 0 lined up with it. When it swings up and down the same way as the nearest pivot underneath it, with or without something sliding in between, gravity acts on the sum of their angles. The motor controller only knows this mechanism's angle, so kG is worked out on the roboRIO each loop instead and sent with the setpoint. A turret or elevator underneath doesn't change gravity.

      Overrides:
      setParent in class MechanismBase
      Parameters:
      parent - What it's mounted on
